checks.title: Pure-solid standard state
checks.focus: Pure-solid unit activity; subcooled pure-liquid standard state; equality of chemical potentials and phase amount distinction.
checks.expected_narration: We begin with a solid and a liquid at equilibrium. The chemical potential of the component must be the same in the two present phases. On the liquid side, we write its chemical potential as the pure-liquid reference plus R T times the natural logarithm of x times gamma. The reference is the subcooled pure liquid at the same temperature and pressure. That reference may be a hypothetical continuation below the melting temperature, but it defines the activity convention consistently. The pure solid has unit activity on its own standard state. Unit activity does not mean that its chemical potential or amount is zero. The equality determines a liquid activity. Determining how many moles occupy each phase still requires a material balance.

checks.title: Finite-vessel inventory
checks.focus: Psub V/(RT), finite gas capacity and min inventory; partial versus total pressure; mu_g minus mu_s over RT equals ln(pA/Psub), negative after exhaustion.
checks.expected_narration: Start the vessel calculation by finding the gas capacity at sublimation equilibrium. Multiply sublimation pressure by accessible gas volume, then divide by R T. Compare that capacity with the total amount of the subliming species. Gas moles equal the smaller of the available inventory and that capacity. Solid moles are the remaining inventory. Use gas moles in the ideal-gas equation to obtain the species partial pressure, and add the inert contribution only when calculating total pressure. With kilopascals and liters, R has the numerical value eight point three one four four six in compatible units. The gas chemical potential minus the pure-solid reference, divided by R T, is the natural logarithm of partial pressure divided by sublimation pressure. Zero applies with present solid. A negative value is allowed after solid exhaustion.

The free gas volume is the space available to the gas. In this teaching model we neglect the solid volume. Keep the declared temperature interval from two hundred fifty to three hundred fifty kelvin. The source field identifies these numbers as synthetic teaching definitions rather than measured properties of a real chemical. The reference temperature is also three hundred kelvin. checks.title: Langmuir model
checks.focus: Langmuir denominator one plus bP; finite saturation uptake, reciprocal-pressure b and dimensionless fractional coverage.
checks.expected_narration: The Langmuir equation writes uptake as the saturation uptake multiplied by b P, divided by one plus b P. Saturation uptake has units of moles per kilogram. The parameter b has reciprocal-pressure units, so the product b P is dimensionless. The ratio of uptake to saturation uptake is the fractional coverage in this model. It rises from zero toward one as pressure increases. At b P equal to one, the coverage is one half. The idealized interpretation involves a finite set of equivalent sites without lateral interactions. These assumptions help us understand the equation, but fitting the equation successfully does not establish a microscopic mechanism. Later, we will use it as a specified synthetic model and check its consequences through a vessel balance.
checks.recognized: The Langmuir equation writes uptake as the saturation uptake multiplied by Bp, divided by 1 plus Bp. Saturation uptake has units of moles per kilogram. The parameter B has reciprocal pressure units, so the product Bp is dimensionless. The ratio of uptake to saturation uptake is the fractional coverage in this model. It rises from zero toward one as pressure increases. At Bp equal to one, the coverage is one half. The idealized interpretation involves a finite set of equivalent sites without lateral interactions. These assumptions help us understand the equation, but fitting the equation successfully does not establish a microscopic mechanism. Later, we will use it as a specified synthetic model and check its consequences through a vessel balance.

At ten kilopascals, with saturation uptake two and b equal to zero point one per kilopascal, the Langmuir uptake is one mole per kilogram. Adding them gives a required total inventory of about zero point zero one four zero zero nine moles. checks.expected_narration: We are now in the real Lab eleven interface. Keep worksheet page five and Lab guide pages three and four open. Begin in Explore isotherms, the upper calculator. The data fitting section lower on the page is optional for this lesson. Our main task is to compare two adsorption models and close a vessel balance. The chart displays four model curves, but the model selected in the menu is the one used to solve the closed vessel. The other curves are not additional phases and are not combined into that balance. Select Langmuir and check a capacity of two moles per kilogram and an affinity of zero point one per kilopascal. Use three hundred kelvin. The pressure units matter because the product of affinity and pressure must be dimensionless. Entering a pressure in pascals while retaining an affinity per kilopascal would change that product by a factor of one thousand. Identify the parameters as synthetic definitions at this temperature. Changing the temperature field does not generate a new temperature dependent parameter set. For our first comparison, set the minimum pressure to zero and the maximum to ten kilopascals so that the lower pressure curves are easy to see. The worksheet uses zero to one hundred kilopascals for your independent investigation. All three vessel roots are below ten kilopascals, so either admitted window gives the same roots. We will widen the range later. Expand Closed vessel, fixed temperature and free gas volume. Enter one liter of free gas volume, ten grams of dry adsorbent, zero point zero one zero mole of total adsorbate, and zero inert gas. This total inventory is the one used in the Lab investigation. It is different from the earlier worked example in which a pressure of ten kilopascals was given and the required total inventory was calculated. Here the pressure is unknown.
